subject: Per-token proration, streaming windowing, and tier structure clarification
messages:

Cc: James Phillips <james.phillips@aurelia-health.com>, procurement@aurelia-health.com

Subject: Clarify per-token billing for streaming & commit tiers

Naomi —

Thanks for the demo this week. A couple of questions came up from our procurement/legal team about how Redwood measures billable tokens for long-lived streaming connections (we use streaming for real-time clinical summary aggregation). Specifically:

- If a single streaming session produces intermittent tokens over several minutes, do you bill per-final-response token or do you aggregate over the session?
- How do you round/quantize chargeable units for streaming? (e.g., per-second, per-token, 1s windows, or some other slab)
- For committed monthly volumes, what happens when streaming bursts push us over a tier mid-billing period — is proration applied or do you bill at the higher slab for the entire period?

Legal would like a short, plain‑language definition we can include in the SOW so the contract explicitly captures the metering approach. Could you provide a few options (conservative/market-standard/preferred) and the downstream billing impact so we can fast-track procurement?

We need this by EOD Wednesday if possible — the procurement deadline is tight.

Appreciate it,
Alice
Senior Procurement Manager
Aurelia Health

Hi Alice —

Thanks — and great question. We discussed this with finance/legal and prepared three contract-aligned options for how to express streaming billable units in the SOW. Each option has different trade-offs for predictability and price. I attached the pricing matrix so you can see the cost impact per 100k tokens under each approach. Summary below:

Option A (Preferred — industry-friendly, cost-stable):
- Billable tokens = request tokens + response tokens (same definition as non-streaming).
- Streaming sessions are billed by aggregating tokens across the session. No additional per-second slab is applied.
- Rounding: bill to the nearest 1,000 tokens per usage event (monthly aggregation).
- Commit behavior: usage applied against monthly commit; overage billed at overage rate. No retroactive upgrade to a higher slab mid-month.

Option B (Conservative — simpler for high-frequency short bursts):
- Billable tokens = request tokens + response tokens, but streaming bursts are sampled into 1-second windows. Each 1-second window is rounded up to 1,000 tokens for billing to avoid microbilling on chattier streams.
- Commit behavior: if monthly usage crosses a higher tier, proration applies to the incremental tokens above the committed bucket for that billing period.

Option C (Customer-favorable — predictable all-in tiers):
- Billable tokens measured as total tokens (no windowing); Redwood will apply monthly smoothing to even out burstiness.
- Pricing: if a customer hits a higher slab during the month, we retroactively apply the higher slab pricing to all usage that month but provide a true-up credit on the following invoice if usage normalizes (suitable for large strategic customers).

Recommended next step: tell me which option you prefer and we will send a clean SOW paragraph and a short clause for the MSA. If helpful, finance can model estimated monthly invoices using your sample audit_log.csv to show dollars at stake.

Best,
Naomi

Naomi / Marcus —

Commercial thoughts quick:
- Option A is the lowest friction and the easiest to explain to procurement. It preserves our standing pricing and avoids mid-month administrative complexity. Recommend we lead with A.
- Option B (1s windowing + 1k-token rounding per window) materially increases billable tokens for chattier streams; if Aurelia's traffic profile is many small response fragments, that could be a meaningful uplift. If they push for B, counter with: 1s windowing but round monthly (aggregate windows into monthly total then round once) — preserves predictability and controls microbilling.
- Option C is fine as a high-touch concession for a strategic account but should require a committed higher monthly spend and a 12-month term.

Negotiation play: lead with Option A in the SOW. Offer Option B (monthly-window aggregation) as an alternate appendix for streaming-heavy pipelines, explicitly capped by a percentage uplift (e.g., no more than +15% billable tokens vs. baseline model) based on their sample log we already have. That cap makes procurement comfortable.

I drafted a short clause below you can drop in the SOW. Marcus please review for legalese.

Proposed SOW paragraph (commercial draft):
"Billable Units and Streaming Sessions: Billable units are defined as the sum of request tokens and response tokens generated by API calls (\"Billable Tokens\"). For streaming sessions, Billable Tokens will be aggregated across the lifetime of the session and reported on a monthly basis. For invoicing, monthly Billable Tokens will be rounded to the nearest 1,000 tokens. Commit volumes will be consumed on a monthly basis; any usage above committed monthly volumes will be charged at the agreed overage rate. For customers with streaming-heavy workloads, an alternate aggregation method (per-second windowing with monthly aggregation and rounding) may be applied by mutual agreement and documented in the SOW appendix."

Let me know and I can send to Alice with the pricing impact table.

-Ben
Director, Commercial Operations

Ben/Naomi —

Legal OK to use Ben's paragraph with two small edits for clarity and to avoid ambiguity in the MSA:
1) Replace "nearest 1,000 tokens" with "1,000-token increments" and clarify that rounding applies after monthly aggregation.
2) Add an explicit statement that no retroactive reclassification of a billing month will be performed (i.e., if a higher slab is reached mid-month, the month shall be billed according to the monthly aggregation and the agreed slab/pricing for that month; true-ups may be scheduled for subsequent billing cycles only if separately agreed).

Final suggested language (legal-ready):
"Billable Units and Streaming Sessions: For purposes of this Agreement, \"Billable Tokens\" means the aggregate number of request and response tokens generated by Customer's API usage during a calendar month. Streaming sessions will be measured by aggregating tokens emitted for the duration of each session and then summing across all sessions for the calendar month. Monthly Billable Tokens will be rounded in 1,000-token increments after aggregation. Commit volumes shall be applied on a monthly basis; usage in excess of committed monthly volumes will be invoiced at the applicable overage rate. No retroactive reclassification to a different pricing slab will be applied to usage for a completed billing month except where a separate true-up process is expressly documented and agreed in writing"

If you want, I can push this back to procurement as a clean clause and include the pricing matrix.

Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
